title: Ramayana Sells 1.33 Lakh Day One Tickets in National Chains
excerpt: Nitesh Tiwari's epic, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Rama and Yash as Ravana, recorded the PVR Inox and Cinepolis count a week before its November 5 release, with Sacnilk putting all-India Day 1 advance gross at Rs 16.53 crore.
body:
• Ramayana: Part One sold around 1.33 lakh tickets for its opening day in the national chains PVR Inox and Cinepolis as of 11 PM on Thursday, October 29, according to Pinkvilla.
  • The Nitesh Tiwari film, starring Ranbir Kapoor as Rama, Sai Pallavi as Sita and Yash as Ravana, releases in cinemas on Thursday, November 5, a week after the count was taken.
  • Sacnilk's all-India tracker put total Day 1 advance gross at Rs 16.53 crore (Rs 13.69 crore excluding blocked seats) from 3.22 lakh tickets across 6,599 shows.
  • Full advance booking has yet to open in non-national chains, single screens and parts of the South Indian market, so the national-chain figure is an early, partial read.

Nitesh Tiwari's Ramayana: Part One has sold around 1.33 lakh tickets for its opening day in India's top two national chains, PVR Inox and Cinepolis, as of 11 PM on Thursday, October 29, according to Pinkvilla. The film, starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash, releases on Thursday, November 5, which means the count was recorded a full week before the first show.

Pinkvilla described the pre-sales as a healthy head start rather than a finished picture. The full-fledged advance booking is yet to open in non-national chains, single screens and South Indian markets, three segments that can change the all-India opening-day picture substantially once they come on stream.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=1XmK81k9qY4

What the wider tracker shows

The national-chain number sits inside a larger all-India advance. Sacnilk's Day 1 advance booking report put the film at Rs 16.53 crore gross, or Rs 13.69 crore excluding blocked seats, from 3.22 lakh tickets booked across 6,599 shows at 709 cinemas in 202 cities. Karnataka was the biggest state at Rs 3.39 crore, followed by Maharashtra at Rs 3.26 crore and Delhi at Rs 2.96 crore.

The language split underlines where the demand is concentrated. Hindi accounted for Rs 13.72 crore of the Day 1 gross, about 83 percent, while Kannada contributed Rs 2.27 crore. Premium formats punched above their weight: Sacnilk reported that premium formats such as IMAX and 4DX held 26 percent of the gross from only 5 percent of shows, with a Hindi IMAX 3D ticket averaging Rs 1,130 against Rs 492 for Hindi 3D.

The film behind the numbers

Ramayana: Part One is directed by Nitesh Tiwari and produced by Namit Malhotra. Ranbir Kapoor plays Lord Rama, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Yash plays Ravana and Sunny Deol plays Hanuman, according to The Hollywood Reporter India. It is the first instalment of a planned two-part adaptation of the epic. Yash is also a co-producer alongside Malhotra and, through the distribution arm of his banner Monster Mind Creations, is handling the film's theatrical distribution in Karnataka.

The advance did not start with this week's count. The Hollywood Reporter India reported on October 26 that worldwide advance bookings, including paid previews, had already crossed $2 million, at approximately $2.15 million or Rs 20.50 crore at that point. Within that total, North American paid previews scheduled for November 4 had generated more than $550,000, and overseas markets outside North America had added over $400,000 for November 5 shows.

Why the final stretch decides it

Trade trackers caution against reading a week-out chain total as an opening-day forecast. Pinkvilla noted that what matters most in pre-sales is the final stretch, from the Monday before release to the day before release, and that the day before release can at times change the entire outlook of the advance. By that Monday, the film will also have a direct comparison available in Dhurandhar: The Revenge, which opened general weekend sales four days prior to its release.

For diaspora audiences, the North American preview figure is the number to watch. Paid previews on November 4 had already passed $550,000 by October 26, before the final-week push in the United States and Canada had begun. Whether Ramayana converts its Indian multiplex start into a comparable overseas opening will be clearer once single screens, non-national chains and the remaining South Indian bookings are counted in the last four days before November 5.
